answer: In this PoA design, bonded collateral escrows make each identity costly to operate, while correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers penalties across their pairwise relationships, scaling as O(k²). A sybil operator therefore cannot divide risk harmlessly among aliases: detection compounds the quadratic slash with an exponential multiplier in capital loss. Asymmetric depreciation further limits recovery; identities may wander from a meadow of apparent safety, but sable-like concealment does not reduce shared evidence or liability.
